$comment: P68 round 9 (lane `cs`) — D-C-INCOMPATIBLE-POINTER-CONVERSION-REFUSED-WHERE-EVERY-REFERENCE-WARNS, with D-CSUBSET-INCOMPATIBLE-ELEMENT-ARRAY-TERNARY's `?:` arm. A pointer mixed with a pointer to an INCOMPATIBLE type, or with an integer that is not a null pointer constant, is a C constraint violation — a diagnostic is owed, nothing more — at every site of the pointer-compatibility constraint, and this one translation unit visits every site: initialization (a local, a brace ELEMENT the HIR lowering reports), assignment, argument, return, `==`, and the arms of `?:`. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23, each reference separately, the file itself compiled and RUN: gcc 13.3.0 and mingw-w64 13.2.0 at -std=c2x and MSVC 19.51 at /std:c17 and /std:clatest build it with a warning per site and exit 42; clang 18.1.3 refuses its integer/pointer and function-signature mixes by default (it builds the object-pointer pairs); gcc and clang at -std=c17 -pedantic-errors refuse, the required diagnostic made an error. DSS warns at each of the 13 positions below — S_IncompatiblePointerConversion for incompatible pointer types (the `?:` and `==` sites included), S_IncompatiblePointerIntegerPointee for the one pair of distinct integer types sharing a representation, S_IntegerPointerConversion for the integer/pointer pair — builds it, and every pointer keeps its value; the `?:` of `int *` and `float *` arms is a `void *` (gcc's and clang's meaning; MSVC types it as the second arm). ★ ONE WARNING LIST HOLDS ON EVERY TARGET: the same-representation pair is chosen per data model (`__LP64__` is declared by the object format), and every other pair differs in more than a name on every model. `--warnings-as-errors` turns every one back into a refusal (GCC 14's default). exit 42 = every converted pointer read or wrote the object it had to; see main.c for the per-shape sum.
